react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converge on Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260 / hsa00260) as the primary affected pathway. RaMP multi-DB ORA ranks it first with FDR=1.3×10⁻⁸ and fold-enrichment=758, driven by L-threonine (KEGG:C00188), L-glutamic acid (KEGG:C00025), choline (KEGG:C00114), and dihydrolipoate (KEGG:C02147). Mummichog m/z-direct activity also ranks the equivalent pathway #1 (p=0.003, 6 of 6 matched metabolites), independently confirming the signal without annotation-reliance. MetaboAnalystR KEGG ORA places hsa00260 at the top (p=0.004), with choline and L-threonine as overlapping compounds. A secondary consensus emerges around nicotinamide (niacinamide, KEGG:C00153) and L-glutamic acid: RaMP links them to Nicotinate and nicotinamide metabolism (KEGG:map00760, FDR=7.0×10⁻⁴) and MetaboAnalystR hits the same KEGG entry hsa00760 (p=0.046), while Mummichog independently scores the equivalent network module #2 (p=0.0098). The driver metabolites trace to two metabolic hubs: (1) the glycine/serine/threonine cluster centred on L-threonine catabolism and one-carbon transfer reactions involving dihydrolipoate as a cofactor, and (2) the NAD⁺-precursor arm centred on niacinamide and L-glutamic acid which donates the amino group in de novo NAD⁺ biosynthesis. Choline (KEGG:C00114) participates in both serine-choline interconversion and glycerophospholipid remodelling. Pyruvic acid (C00022), oxoglutaric acid (C00026), and phosphate (C00009) are consistent with altered glycolytic/TCA flux and kinase-mediated signalling, though they do not individually meet single-pathway ORA significance thresholds at this sample size. The cross-paradigm replication across ORA, m/z-activity, and network-diffusion contexts substantially strengthens confidence that amino-acid catabolism and NAD⁺-related metabolism are mechanistically perturbed in the treatment condition.
